summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee reviewed logistics for First Day celebrations, light displays, parade cannons, and event reimbursement guidelines.
summary.summary: The Southborough Tricentennial Committee met to advance preparations for the town's upcoming 300th anniversary events, focusing heavily on First Day activities scheduled for January 1. Key plans reviewed included the coordination of a 15-minute drone show, fire pits run by Boy Scouts, a 300-stone commemorative project, and parade artillery logistics. The committee also worked through sponsorship outreach, tree lighting around the Town House and library, and an administrative procedure for member reimbursements and invoice payments.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from October 14, 2026, with minor typographical corrections to member names. At the end of the meeting, the committee voted to adjourn.
key_details: Minutes of October 14, 2026 approved.

topics.title: Awareness days and business promotion
topics.summary: Members discussed balancing promotion between major tricentennial sponsors and general Southborough small businesses on social media. The plan is to provide dedicated spotlight posts for sponsors while featuring roundups of all local businesses periodically.
key_details: Plan includes monthly posts highlighting groups of Southborough small businesses.
Major sponsors will continue to receive individual dedicated spotlight posts.
topics.outcome: Plan noted with ongoing social media rollout.

topics.title: History in Bloom project update
topics.summary: The committee noted that the planned fall planting of flower bulbs could not be completed because the coordination window with the Department of Public Works was too narrow. As an alternative, flowers will be planted directly in the spring.
key_details: Fall bulb planting cancelled due to scheduling constraints.
Spring planting will replace the fall bulb initiative.
topics.outcome: Spring flower planting adopted as the alternative.

topics.title: School history tours and event registration setup
topics.summary: The committee reviewed registration setups in the Bloomerang platform for guided history tours at St. Mark's School and Fay School. Members addressed details such as four separate time slots for St. Mark's, email confirmations and cancellation workflows, and collecting participant addresses for events prioritizing Southborough residents.
key_details: St. Mark's tours will feature four separate time slots.
Fay School tour will run in a single time slot.
Participant addresses will be collected to verify town residency where required.
Liability waiver forms will be incorporated into the registration process.
topics.outcome: Registration forms to be finalized and tested through Bloomerang.

topics.title: Music festival and Voices from the Grave updates
topics.summary: Members received brief reports on music festival planning and the cemetery theater production Voices from the Grave. Music staging arrangements await finalization of the headlining act's contract, while Voices from the Grave continues casting calls for local actors.
key_details: Music stage contracting is waiting on performer contract finalization.
Voices from the Grave organizers are continuing to recruit local actors.

topics.title: History Makers nominations
topics.summary: A working group reviewed the 26 community nominations submitted for the History Makers recognition program. The committee plans to announce 15 final award categories in January and acknowledge all nominees publicly.
key_details: 26 total nominations received.
Recipients will be recognized across 15 categories.
Public announcements scheduled for January.
topics.outcome: Categories to be finalized for January announcement.

topics.title: History Talks, House Tour, and parade artillery
topics.summary: Planning was reviewed for a January 1 history talk by Nick Noble, including book sales to benefit the Historical Commission's sign program. The committee also discussed parade logistics involving Crane's Artillery, which plans to fire blank cannon shots during the parade from the high ground off Route 85, along with coordinating public safety and pet warnings.
key_details: Nick Noble talk set for 3:00 PM on January 1, followed by a reception.
Cannon firing location proposed on high ground near Route 85 firing toward trees away from spectators.
Estimated cannon firing cost is roughly $100 per blank shot.
Committee will coordinate safety with police and warn residents about noise for pets and sensitive individuals.
topics.outcome: Site coordination and safety plans to be reviewed with public safety officials.

topics.title: First Day (January 1) celebration logistics
topics.summary: The committee reviewed plans for First Day celebrations on January 1, 2027. Topics included engaging Indigenous representatives from the Hassanamisco Nipmuc Band, coordinating a 15-minute drone show set to music, arranging Boy Scout barrel fires with s'mores packages, and distributing 300 commemorative stones marked with years from 1727 to 2027.
key_details: Correspondence received from the Hassanamisco Nipmuc Band regarding municipal event participation criteria.
Four student artwork submissions will be incorporated into the drone show imagery.
Police detail for First Day agreed at four officers for four hours (2:00 PM to 6:00 PM) at roughly $1,118.
Boy Scouts will operate barrel fires outside with adult supervision and sell s'mores packages.
300 painted river stones representing each town year will be created, with some retained at the Senior Center.
topics.outcome: Organizers authorized to proceed with event arrangements and police details.

topics.title: Firemen's Muster event coordination
topics.summary: The committee discussed logistics for the hand tub Firemen's Muster. The Fire Department has agreed to supply the water using a tanker rig to fill the pumping basin. Organizers are also coordinating food trucks, musical entertainment, and a makers market for the event.
key_details: Fire Department will supply water tanker support for hand tub pumping.
Food trucks and one dessert vendor are being recruited.
Detailed operational calculations and field layout will be reviewed with town officials.
topics.outcome: Draft layout and logistics plan to be shared with town facilities and safety staff.

topics.title: Tricentennial time capsule
topics.summary: The time capsule working group reported that it is developing criteria for submitted items, favoring archival-grade digital media alongside physical artifacts and an oral history component. Outreach to historic local businesses for contributions will begin soon.
key_details: Working group will hold its first formal meeting within two weeks.
Content will include both physical memorabilia and digital archival media.
An oral history project documenting town memories may be included.
topics.outcome: Working group to convene and build a formal acquisition schedule.

topics.title: Glow SoBo decorative tree lighting
topics.summary: Members discussed commercial holiday lighting on trees and shrubs in front of the Town House and library for the Glow SoBo initiative. Because a tree at the Town House is being removed, the scope of work is being adjusted to light bushes on either side of the Town House entrance plus three trees at the library.
key_details: Original estimate for lighting six trees was approximately $10,000.
Lighting scope adjusted due to removal of a Town House tree; will cover two entrance bushes and three library trees.
Electrical service connections at historic town buildings are being inspected.
A local landscaping company has offered to meet to discuss lighting services.
topics.outcome: Working group will obtain revised pricing based on the updated tree count.

topics.title: Incorporation Day ceremony
topics.summary: The committee reviewed preliminary outlines for the official Incorporation Day ceremony, including coordination with town administration and the Select Board regarding dates and venue. Discussions also touched upon musical accompaniment options.
key_details: Ceremony outline shared with the town administrator for initial review.
Local musician may perform during the Incorporation Day ceremony and the music festival.
topics.outcome: Staff will arrange an upcoming meeting with the town administrator.

topics.title: Utility pole banner installation
topics.summary: The committee received an update on placing 50 commemorative banners on utility poles. Verizon and the town must conduct a physical inspection of the designated poles. The committee discussed purchasing two initial sample banners for display behind the Town House and reviewed options for bucket truck contractor services to install them along main roads.
key_details: Verizon pole inspection requires a town representative to accompany inspectors across 50 poles.
Two sample banners will be ordered first for test installation behind the Town House.
A bucket truck contractor or DPW assistance will be required to safely hang banners on busy roadways.
topics.outcome: The chair will accompany Verizon on pole inspections and coordinate installation resources.

topics.title: Legacy Trees donation
topics.summary: The Tree Warden and the committee confirmed selections and locations for four legacy trees to mark the tricentennial. The trees are being donated by Shrubs and Trees on Route 9, and granite marker prototypes will be presented for review.
key_details: Selected species include a red maple in Southville, a littleleaf linden in Fayville, and a red oak on the Town Common, among four total trees.
All four trees are donated in kind by Shrubs and Trees on Route 9.
Granite commemorative ground markers will be designed for each tree.
topics.outcome: Tree selections confirmed; marker prototypes to be submitted for approval.

topics.title: Brick fundraiser and sponsorship letters
topics.summary: The committee discussed extending the commemorative brick fundraiser through the end of the month. Members addressed delays in mailing sponsorship appeal letters to local small businesses due to list coordination issues.
key_details: Brick sales anticipated to close at month's end.
Business sponsorship letter template is drafted and awaiting final mailing list distribution.
topics.outcome: Committee members to coordinate mailing list compilation outside the meeting.

topics.title: Expenditure and reimbursement policy
topics.summary: The committee reviewed a standard expense reimbursement policy and form for committee expenditures. Members debated whether expenditures within previously approved event budgets require full committee votes or can be approved by the chair and vice chair. The committee agreed that expenses already within approved event line items can be processed directly by the chair and vice chair, while any expenses exceeding an approved budget or entering new major contracts must come before the full committee.
key_details: Standardized PDF expense submission form introduced for member receipts.
Expenses exceeding approved event budgets must receive full committee approval.
Routine budgeted expenses may be authorized by the chair or vice chair directly.
topics.outcome: Reimbursement policy language to be amended and submitted to town administration.

topics.title: AI transcription trial for meeting minutes
topics.summary: A member presented a demonstration plan to test AI transcription tools (Granola and Claude) to assist in drafting future meeting minutes. The committee agreed to run the software alongside human-drafted minutes to evaluate accuracy, noting that human proofreading and official public record disclosures will remain mandatory.
key_details: AI software to be tested as an assistive drafting tool at no cost to the town.
Committee minutes will continue to be reviewed, proofread, and approved by committee members.
A comparison test will be run using recorded video from upcoming meetings.
topics.outcome: AI transcription software to be tested on a trial basis.
